# Linux Container Primitives — Vault Notes

## The Core Mental Model

* **Containers do not exist as a single kernel primitive [[01:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D75)]:** A "container" is simply a standard Linux process isolated and constrained by combining three independent kernel primitives:
1. **Control Groups (cgroups):** Resource accounting, limits, and prioritization.
2. **Namespaces:** Visibility and access boundaries (what the process can see).
3. **Layered File Systems (OverlayFS):** Copy-on-write image composition and root filesystem isolation.



---

## 1. Control Groups (cgroups): Resource Management

cgroups track, group, and limit resource consumption across process trees [[02:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D139)]. Every process on a modern Linux system belongs to a cgroup hierarchy regardless of whether it runs in a container.

* **Subsystem Hierarchies [[02:49](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D169)]:** Subsystems (CPU, memory, pids, devices, blkio) maintain independent trees. This enables flexible configuration (e.g., two processes can share a memory pool while having unequal CPU shares).
* **Inheritance [[04:06](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D246)]:** Child processes automatically inherit the cgroup membership of their parent.
* **Virtual VFS Interface [[04:12](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D252)]:** Managed via `/sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/`.
* `tasks` / `cgroup.procs`: Holds assigned PIDs. Writing a PID into this file moves the target process into that cgroup [[04:43](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D283)].
* `pids.max`: Limits max concurrent processes to prevent resource exhaustion attacks like fork bombs [[07:34](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D454)].
* `cpu.shares`: Proportional weight for CPU time distribution [[09:01](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D541)].


* **Introspection [[05:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D348)]:** A process's assigned cgroups can be inspected at `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`.

---

## 2. Namespaces: Boundary & Visibility Control

Namespaces restrict what a process can see and access, creating the illusion that each container has its own dedicated system resources [[10:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D618)].

### Core Namespaces Used in Containers

* **Network (`net`) [[11:24](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D684)]:** Independent network devices, IP routing tables, port bindings, and firewall rules. Connected to host bridges (e.g., `docker0`) via virtual Ethernet (`veth`) pairs.
* **Mount (`mnt`) [[12:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D723)]:** Dedicated filesystem mount points, hiding the host filesystem and presenting an isolated rootfs.
* **PID (`pid`):** Independent process tree where the root container process runs as PID 1.
* User (`user`), IPC (`ipc`), UTS (`uts`), Time (`time`) [[10:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D650)].

### Namespace Syscalls & Lifecycle

* **`clone(..., CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:16](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D796)]:** Spawns a child process directly inside a new set of namespaces.
* **`unshare(CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:28](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D808)]:** Disassociates the calling process from its current namespaces and creates new ones.
* **`setns(fd, nstype)` [[14:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D857)]:** Attaches a process to an existing namespace using an open file descriptor from `/proc/<pid>/ns/*` or a persistent bind mount.
* **Persistence Mechanism [[13:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D828)]:** Namespaces terminate when no active processes or references remain. To keep an empty namespace alive, create a bind mount of its `/proc/<pid>/ns/<type>` symlink (e.g., into `/var/run/netns/` for `ip netns` management).

---

## 3. Union Filesystems & OverlayFS: Layer Storage

Container images act as layered archives providing a Copy-on-Write (CoW) unified filesystem view [[21:30](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1290)].

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Merged View (/merged)                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  UpperDir (Writable Container Layer)                    │
│    ├── Modified files (copied up)                       │
│    └── Whiteouts (char dev 0:0 for deleted files)       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LowerDir (Read-Only Image Layers, stacked)             │
│    ├── Layer 2 (Application code/diff)                 │
│    └── Layer 1 (Base OS / rootfs)                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

* **OverlayFS Components [[22:33](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1353)]:**
* `lowerdir`: Read-only base layers stacked sequentially.
* `upperdir`: Single read-write layer where runtime file changes land.
* `workdir`: Scratch directory used by the kernel for atomic operations during copy-up.
* `merged`: Mount target presenting the composite file tree.


* **Copy-Up Performance Cost [[23:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1380)]:** When a file in `lowerdir` is opened for writing, the entire file is copied up to `upperdir` before the `open()` syscall returns. Large files incur significant I/O latency and consume double disk space even if modifying a single byte.
* **Deletions & Whiteouts [[23:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1395)]:** Deleting a file from a lower layer does not remove it from disk; instead, OverlayFS writes a special character device (`0,0`) into `upperdir` to mask the lower file.
* **Docker Layout [[24:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1458)]:** Stored in `/var/lib/docker/overlay2/` using shortened layer symlinks (`/l/`) to stay within kernel mount option string length limits [[29:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1790)].

---

## 4. Container Runtimes & The OCI Standard

* **Container Runtime Definition [[31:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1860)]:** Host software that orchestrates cgroups, namespaces, and mounts to launch isolated processes.
* **OCI Runtime Specification [[31:23](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1883)]:** Standardized runtime interfaces and container bundle formats.
* **Bundle Structure [[31:51](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1911)]:** Consists of a root filesystem directory (`rootfs`) + a `config.json` file defining user, environment variables, capabilities, mounts, and lifecycle hooks.


* **Reference Implementation (`runc`) [[31:36](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1896)]:** Donated by Docker; used as the low-level executor by `containerd`, `CRI-O`, and Docker.
* **Lifecycle Hooks [[32:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1939)]:** Allows external tools to mutate filesystems or attach configurations before start (`prestart`), after start (`poststart`), and after exit (`poststop`).

---

| --- | --- |

## Takeaways & Gotchas

* **Hidden disk bloat:** Removing files in upper Dockerfile layers does not reduce image size because lower layer data remains intact beneath whiteout markers [[27:42](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1662)].

* **Mount (`mnt`) [[12:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D723)]:** Dedicated filesystem mount points, hiding the host filesystem and presenting an isolated rootfs.
* **PID (`pid`):** Independent process tree where the root container process runs as PID 1.
* User (`user`), IPC (`ipc`), UTS (`uts`), Time (`time`) [[10:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D650)].

### Namespace Syscalls & Lifecycle

* **`clone(..., CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:16](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D796)]:** Spawns a child process directly inside a new set of namespaces.
* **`unshare(CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:28](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D808)]:** Disassociates the calling process from its current namespaces and creates new ones.
* **`setns(fd, nstype)` [[14:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D857)]:** Attaches a process to an existing namespace using an open file descriptor from `/proc/<pid>/ns/*` or a persistent bind mount.
* **Persistence Mechanism [[13:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D828)]:** Namespaces terminate when no active processes or references remain. To keep an empty namespace alive, create a bind mount of its `/proc/<pid>/ns/<type>` symlink (e.g., into `/var/run/netns/` for `ip netns` management).

---

## 3. Union Filesystems & OverlayFS: Layer Storage

Container images act as layered archives providing a Copy-on-Write (CoW) unified filesystem view [[21:30](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1290)].

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Merged View (/merged)                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  UpperDir (Writable Container Layer)                    │
│    ├── Modified files (copied up)                       │
│    └── Whiteouts (char dev 0:0 for deleted files)       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LowerDir (Read-Only Image Layers, stacked)             │
│    ├── Layer 2 (Application code/diff)                 │
│    └── Layer 1 (Base OS / rootfs)                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

* **OverlayFS Components [[22:33](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1353)]:**
* `lowerdir`: Read-only base layers stacked sequentially.
* `upperdir`: Single read-write layer where runtime file changes land.
* `workdir`: Scratch directory used by the kernel for atomic operations during copy-up.
* `merged`: Mount target presenting the composite file tree.


* **Copy-Up Performance Cost [[23:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1380)]:** When a file in `lowerdir` is opened for writing, the entire file is copied up to `upperdir` before the `open()` syscall returns. Large files incur significant I/O latency and consume double disk space even if modifying a single byte.
* **Deletions & Whiteouts [[23:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1395)]:** Deleting a file from a lower layer does not remove it from disk; instead, OverlayFS writes a special character device (`0,0`) into `upperdir` to mask the lower file.
* **Docker Layout [[24:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1458)]:** Stored in `/var/lib/docker/overlay2/` using shortened layer symlinks (`/l/`) to stay within kernel mount option string length limits [[29:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1790)].

---

## 4. Container Runtimes & The OCI Standard

* **Container Runtime Definition [[31:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1860)]:** Host software that orchestrates cgroups, namespaces, and mounts to launch isolated processes.
* **OCI Runtime Specification [[31:23](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1883)]:** Standardized runtime interfaces and container bundle formats.
* **Bundle Structure [[31:51](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1911)]:** Consists of a root filesystem directory (`rootfs`) + a `config.json` file defining user, environment variables, capabilities, mounts, and lifecycle hooks.


* **Reference Implementation (`runc`) [[31:36](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1896)]:** Donated by Docker; used as the low-level executor by `containerd`, `CRI-O`, and Docker.
* **Lifecycle Hooks [[32:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1939)]:** Allows external tools to mutate filesystems or attach configurations before start (`prestart`), after start (`poststart`), and after exit (`poststop`).

---

## Quick Command & Troubleshooting Reference

| Objective | Command / Interface |
| --- | --- |
| Inspect cgroups of a running process | `cat /proc/<PID>/cgroup` [[06:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D363)] |
| Move process to a cgroup | `echo <PID> >> /sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/<group>/tasks` [[06:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D406)] |
| Inspect namespace symlinks | `ls -l /proc/<PID>/ns/` [[12:41](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D761)] |
| Run shell in isolated net namespace | `unshare --net /bin/bash` [[15:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D917)] |
| Enter container namespace from host | `nsenter --target <PID> --mount --net -- /bin/bash` [[19:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1186)] |
| Manage persistent net namespace | `ip netns add <name>` / `ip netns exec <name> <cmd>` [[16:25](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D985)] |

---

## Takeaways & Gotchas

* **Hidden disk bloat:** Removing files in upper Dockerfile layers does not reduce image size because lower layer data remains intact beneath whiteout markers [[27:42](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1662)].
* **Namespace lifetime gotcha:** If all processes inside a namespace exit and no bind mount exists, the namespace is immediately destroyed by the kernel [[15:35](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D935)].
* **Orchestrator dependencies:** Manually altering cgroup hierarchies on managed nodes can break metrics scrapers like cAdvisor or Amazon ECS agent [[09:54](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D594)].

## To Research / Backlog

* **cgroups v2 unified hierarchy:** Transition from independent subsystem trees to single unified hierarchy with improved resource delegation.
* **Rootless Containers & User Namespaces:** Mapping UID 0 inside a container to an unprivileged UID on the host for enhanced isolation.
* **Time Namespace:** Handling container virtualization of monotonic and boot system clocks [[10:56](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D656)].

## Thoughts / Philosophy

> *"Containers are not monolithic boxes created by virtualization; they are ordinary processes wearing kernel-provided blindfolds (namespaces) and speed limits (cgroups), standing on a layered stack of files (OverlayFS)."*

# Linux Container Primitives — Vault Notes

## The Core Mental Model

* **Containers do not exist as a single kernel primitive [[01:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D75)]:** A "container" is simply a standard Linux process isolated and constrained by combining three independent kernel primitives:
1. **Control Groups (cgroups):** Resource accounting, limits, and prioritization.
2. **Namespaces:** Visibility and access boundaries (what the process can see).
3. **Layered File Systems (OverlayFS):** Copy-on-write image composition and root filesystem isolation.



---

## 1. Control Groups (cgroups): Resource Management

cgroups track, group, and limit resource consumption across process trees [[02:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D139)]. Every process on a modern Linux system belongs to a cgroup hierarchy regardless of whether it runs in a container.

* **Subsystem Hierarchies [[02:49](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D169)]:** Subsystems (CPU, memory, pids, devices, blkio) maintain independent trees. This enables flexible configuration (e.g., two processes can share a memory pool while having unequal CPU shares).
* **Inheritance [[04:06](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D246)]:** Child processes automatically inherit the cgroup membership of their parent.
* **Virtual VFS Interface [[04:12](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D252)]:** Managed via `/sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/`.
* `tasks` / `cgroup.procs`: Holds assigned PIDs. Writing a PID into this file moves the target process into that cgroup [[04:43](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D283)].
* `pids.max`: Limits max concurrent processes to prevent resource exhaustion attacks like fork bombs [[07:34](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D454)].
* `cpu.shares`: Proportional weight for CPU time distribution [[09:01](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D541)].


* **Introspection [[05:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D348)]:** A process's assigned cgroups can be inspected at `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`.

---

## 2. Namespaces: Boundary & Visibility Control

Namespaces restrict what a process can see and access, creating the illusion that each container has its own dedicated system resources [[10:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D618)].

### Core Namespaces Used in Containers

* **Network (`net`) [[11:24](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D684)]:** Independent network devices, IP routing tables, port bindings, and firewall rules. Connected to host bridges (e.g., `docker0`) via virtual Ethernet (`veth`) pairs.
* **Mount (`mnt`) [[12:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D723)]:** Dedicated filesystem mount points, hiding the host filesystem and presenting an isolated rootfs.
* **PID (`pid`):** Independent process tree where the root container process runs as PID 1.
* User (`user`), IPC (`ipc`), UTS (`uts`), Time (`time`) [[10:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D650)].

### Namespace Syscalls & Lifecycle

* **`clone(..., CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:16](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D796)]:** Spawns a child process directly inside a new set of namespaces.
* **`unshare(CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:28](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D808)]:** Disassociates the calling process from its current namespaces and creates new ones.
* **`setns(fd, nstype)` [[14:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D857)]:** Attaches a process to an existing namespace using an open file descriptor from `/proc/<pid>/ns/*` or a persistent bind mount.
* **Persistence Mechanism [[13:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D828)]:** Namespaces terminate when no active processes or references remain. To keep an empty namespace alive, create a bind mount of its `/proc/<pid>/ns/<type>` symlink (e.g., into `/var/run/netns/` for `ip netns` management).

---

## 3. Union Filesystems & OverlayFS: Layer Storage

Container images act as layered archives providing a Copy-on-Write (CoW) unified filesystem view [[21:30](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1290)].

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Merged View (/merged)                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  UpperDir (Writable Container Layer)                    │
│    ├── Modified files (copied up)                       │
│    └── Whiteouts (char dev 0:0 for deleted files)       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LowerDir (Read-Only Image Layers, stacked)             │
│    ├── Layer 2 (Application code/diff)                 │
│    └── Layer 1 (Base OS / rootfs)                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

* **OverlayFS Components [[22:33](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1353)]:**
* `lowerdir`: Read-only base layers stacked sequentially.
* `upperdir`: Single read-write layer where runtime file changes land.
* `workdir`: Scratch directory used by the kernel for atomic operations during copy-up.
* `merged`: Mount target presenting the composite file tree.


* **Copy-Up Performance Cost [[23:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1380)]:** When a file in `lowerdir` is opened for writing, the entire file is copied up to `upperdir` before the `open()` syscall returns. Large files incur significant I/O latency and consume double disk space even if modifying a single byte.
* **Deletions & Whiteouts [[23:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1395)]:** Deleting a file from a lower layer does not remove it from disk; instead, OverlayFS writes a special character device (`0,0`) into `upperdir` to mask the lower file.
* **Docker Layout [[24:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1458)]:** Stored in `/var/lib/docker/overlay2/` using shortened layer symlinks (`/l/`) to stay within kernel mount option string length limits [[29:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1790)].

## 4. Container Runtimes & The OCI Standard

* **Container Runtime Definition [[31:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1860)]:** Host software that orchestrates cgroups, namespaces, and mounts to launch isolated processes.
* **OCI Runtime Specification [[31:23](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1883)]:** Standardized runtime interfaces and container bundle formats.
* **Bundle Structure [[31:51](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1911)]:** Consists of a root filesystem directory (`rootfs`) + a `config.json` file defining user, environment variables, capabilities, mounts, and lifecycle hooks.


* **Reference Implementation (`runc`) [[31:36](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1896)]:** Donated by Docker; used as the low-level executor by `containerd`, `CRI-O`, and Docker.
* **Lifecycle Hooks [[32:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1939)]:** Allows external tools to mutate filesystems or attach configurations before start (`prestart`), after start (`poststart`), and after exit (`poststop`).

---

## 1. Control Groups (cgroups): Resource Management

cgroups track, group, and limit resource consumption across process trees [[02:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D139)]. Every process on a modern Linux system belongs to a cgroup hierarchy regardless of whether it runs in a container.

* **Subsystem Hierarchies [[02:49](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D169)]:** Subsystems (CPU, memory, pids, devices, blkio) maintain independent trees. This enables flexible configuration (e.g., two processes can share a memory pool while having unequal CPU shares).
* **Inheritance [[04:06](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D246)]:** Child processes automatically inherit the cgroup membership of their parent.
* **Virtual VFS Interface [[04:12](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D252)]:** Managed via `/sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/`.
* `tasks` / `cgroup.procs`: Holds assigned PIDs. Writing a PID into this file moves the target process into that cgroup [[04:43](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D283)].
* `pids.max`: Limits max concurrent processes to prevent resource exhaustion attacks like fork bombs [[07:34](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D454)].
* `cpu.shares`: Proportional weight for CPU time distribution [[09:01](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D541)].


* **Introspection [[05:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D348)]:** A process's assigned cgroups can be inspected at `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`.

---

## 2. Namespaces: Boundary & Visibility Control

Namespaces restrict what a process can see and access, creating the illusion that each container has its own dedicated system resources [[10:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D618)].

### Core Namespaces Used in Containers

* **Network (`net`) [[11:24](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D684)]:** Independent network devices, IP routing tables, port bindings, and firewall rules. Connected to host bridges (e.g., `docker0`) via virtual Ethernet (`veth`) pairs.
* **Mount (`mnt`) [[12:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D723)]:** Dedicated filesystem mount points, hiding the host filesystem and presenting an isolated rootfs.
* **PID (`pid`):** Independent process tree where the root container process runs as PID 1.
* User (`user`), IPC (`ipc`), UTS (`uts`), Time (`time`) [[10:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D650)].

### Namespace Syscalls & Lifecycle

* **`clone(..., CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:16](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D796)]:** Spawns a child process directly inside a new set of namespaces.
* **`unshare(CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:28](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D808)]:** Disassociates the calling process from its current namespaces and creates new ones.
* **`setns(fd, nstype)` [[14:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D857)]:** Attaches a process to an existing namespace using an open file descriptor from `/proc/<pid>/ns/*` or a persistent bind mount.
* **Persistence Mechanism [[13:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D828)]:** Namespaces terminate when no active processes or references remain. To keep an empty namespace alive, create a bind mount of its `/proc/<pid>/ns/<type>` symlink (e.g., into `/var/run/netns/` for `ip netns` management).

---

## 3. Union Filesystems & OverlayFS: Layer Storage

Container images act as layered archives providing a Copy-on-Write (CoW) unified filesystem view [[21:30](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1290)].

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Merged View (/merged)                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  UpperDir (Writable Container Layer)                    │
│    ├── Modified files (copied up)                       │
│    └── Whiteouts (char dev 0:0 for deleted files)       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LowerDir (Read-Only Image Layers, stacked)             │
│    ├── Layer 2 (Application code/diff)                 │
│    └── Layer 1 (Base OS / rootfs)                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

* **OverlayFS Components [[22:33](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1353)]:**
* `lowerdir`: Read-only base layers stacked sequentially.
* `upperdir`: Single read-write layer where runtime file changes land.
* `workdir`: Scratch directory used by the kernel for atomic operations during copy-up.
* `merged`: Mount target presenting the composite file tree.


* **Copy-Up Performance Cost [[23:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1380)]:** When a file in `lowerdir` is opened for writing, the entire file is copied up to `upperdir` before the `open()` syscall returns. Large files incur significant I/O latency and consume double disk space even if modifying a single byte.
* **Deletions & Whiteouts [[23:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1395)]:** Deleting a file from a lower layer does not remove it from disk; instead, OverlayFS writes a special character device (`0,0`) into `upperdir` to mask the lower file.
* **Docker Layout [[24:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1458)]:** Stored in `/var/lib/docker/overlay2/` using shortened layer symlinks (`/l/`) to stay within kernel mount option string length limits [[29:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1790)].

---

## 4. Container Runtimes & The OCI Standard

* **Container Runtime Definition [[31:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1860)]:** Host software that orchestrates cgroups, namespaces, and mounts to launch isolated processes.
* **OCI Runtime Specification [[31:23](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1883)]:** Standardized runtime interfaces and container bundle formats.
* **Bundle Structure [[31:51](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1911)]:** Consists of a root filesystem directory (`rootfs`) + a `config.json` file defining user, environment variables, capabilities, mounts, and lifecycle hooks.


* **Reference Implementation (`runc`) [[31:36](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1896)]:** Donated by Docker; used as the low-level executor by `containerd`, `CRI-O`, and Docker.
* **Lifecycle Hooks [[32:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1939)]:** Allows external tools to mutate filesystems or attach configurations before start (`prestart`), after start (`poststart`), and after exit (`poststop`).

---

## Quick Command & Troubleshooting Reference

| Objective | Command / Interface |
| --- | --- |
| Inspect cgroups of a running process | `cat /proc/<PID>/cgroup` [[06:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D363)] |
| Move process to a cgroup | `echo <PID> >> /sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/<group>/tasks` [[06:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D406)] |
| Inspect namespace symlinks | `ls -l /proc/<PID>/ns/` [[12:41](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D761)] |
| Run shell in isolated net namespace | `unshare --net /bin/bash` [[15:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D917)] |
| Enter container namespace from host | `nsenter --target <PID> --mount --net -- /bin/bash` [[19:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1186)] |
| Manage persistent net namespace | `ip netns add <name>` / `ip netns exec <name> <cmd>` [[16:25](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D985)] |

---

## Takeaways & Gotchas

* **Hidden disk bloat:** Removing files in upper Dockerfile layers does not reduce image size because lower layer data remains intact beneath whiteout markers [[27:42](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1662)].
* **Namespace lifetime gotcha:** If all processes inside a namespace exit and no bind mount exists, the namespace is immediately destroyed by the kernel [[15:35](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D935)].
* **Orchestrator dependencies:** Manually altering cgroup hierarchies on managed nodes can break metrics scrapers like cAdvisor or Amazon ECS agent [[09:54](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D594)].

## To Research / Backlog

* **cgroups v2 unified hierarchy:** Transition from independent subsystem trees to single unified hierarchy with improved resource delegation.
* **Rootless Containers & User Namespaces:** Mapping UID 0 inside a container to an unprivileged UID on the host for enhanced isolation.
* **Time Namespace:** Handling container virtualization of monotonic and boot system clocks [[10:56](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D656)].

## Thoughts / Philosophy

> *"Containers are not monolithic boxes created by virtualization; they are ordinary processes wearing kernel-provided blindfolds (namespaces) and speed limits (cgroups), standing on a layered stack of files (OverlayFS)."*

# Linux Container Primitives — Vault Notes

## The Core Mental Model

* **Containers do not exist as a single kernel primitive [[01:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D75)]:** A "container" is simply a standard Linux process isolated and constrained by combining three independent kernel primitives:
1. **Control Groups (cgroups):** Resource accounting, limits, and prioritization.
2. **Namespaces:** Visibility and access boundaries (what the process can see).
3. **Layered File Systems (OverlayFS):** Copy-on-write image composition and root filesystem isolation.



---

This enables flexible configuration (e.g., two processes can share a memory pool while having unequal CPU shares).
* **Inheritance [[04:06](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D246)]:** Child processes automatically inherit the cgroup membership of their parent.
* **Virtual VFS Interface [[04:12](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D252)]:** Managed via `/sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/`.

* **Orchestrator dependencies:** Manually altering cgroup hierarchies on managed nodes can break metrics scrapers like cAdvisor or Amazon ECS agent [[09:54](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D594)].

## To Research / Backlog

* **cgroups v2 unified hierarchy:** Transition from independent subsystem trees to single unified hierarchy with improved resource delegation.
* **Rootless Containers & User Namespaces:** Mapping UID 0 inside a container to an unprivileged UID on the host for enhanced isolation.
* **Time Namespace:** Handling container virtualization of monotonic and boot system clocks [[10:56](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D656)].

## Thoughts / Philosophy

> *"Containers are not monolithic boxes created by virtualization; they are ordinary processes wearing kernel-provided blindfolds (namespaces) and speed limits (cgroups), standing on a layered stack of files (OverlayFS)."*

# Linux Container Primitives — Vault Notes

## The Core Mental Model

* **Containers do not exist as a single kernel primitive [[01:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D75)]:** A "container" is simply a standard Linux process isolated and constrained by combining three independent kernel primitives:
1. **Control Groups (cgroups):** Resource accounting, limits, and prioritization.
2. **Namespaces:** Visibility and access boundaries (what the process can see).
3. **Layered File Systems (OverlayFS):** Copy-on-write image composition and root filesystem isolation.



---

## 1. Control Groups (cgroups): Resource Management

cgroups track, group, and limit resource consumption across process trees [[02:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D139)]. Every process on a modern Linux system belongs to a cgroup hierarchy regardless of whether it runs in a container.

* **Subsystem Hierarchies [[02:49](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D169)]:** Subsystems (CPU, memory, pids, devices, blkio) maintain independent trees. This enables flexible configuration (e.g., two processes can share a memory pool while having unequal CPU shares).
* **Inheritance [[04:06](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D246)]:** Child processes automatically inherit the cgroup membership of their parent.
* **Virtual VFS Interface [[04:12](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D252)]:** Managed via `/sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/`.
* `tasks` / `cgroup.procs`: Holds assigned PIDs. Writing a PID into this file moves the target process into that cgroup [[04:43](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D283)].
* `pids.max`: Limits max concurrent processes to prevent resource exhaustion attacks like fork bombs [[07:34](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D454)].
* `cpu.shares`: Proportional weight for CPU time distribution [[09:01](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D541)].


* **Introspection [[05:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D348)]:** A process's assigned cgroups can be inspected at `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`.

---

## 2. Namespaces: Boundary & Visibility Control

Namespaces restrict what a process can see and access, creating the illusion that each container has its own dedicated system resources [[10:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D618)].

### Core Namespaces Used in Containers

* **Network (`net`) [[11:24](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D684)]:** Independent network devices, IP routing tables, port bindings, and firewall rules. Connected to host bridges (e.g., `docker0`) via virtual Ethernet (`veth`) pairs.
* **Mount (`mnt`) [[12:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D723)]:** Dedicated filesystem mount points, hiding the host filesystem and presenting an isolated rootfs.
* **PID (`pid`):** Independent process tree where the root container process runs as PID 1.
* User (`user`), IPC (`ipc`), UTS (`uts`), Time (`time`) [[10:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D650)].

### Namespace Syscalls & Lifecycle

* **`clone(..., CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:16](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D796)]:** Spawns a child process directly inside a new set of namespaces.
* **`unshare(CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:28](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D808)]:** Disassociates the calling process from its current namespaces and creates new ones.
* **`setns(fd, nstype)` [[14:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D857)]:** Attaches a process to an existing namespace using an open file descriptor from `/proc/<pid>/ns/*` or a persistent bind mount.
* **Persistence Mechanism [[13:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D828)]:** Namespaces terminate when no active processes or references remain. To keep an empty namespace alive, create a bind mount of its `/proc/<pid>/ns/<type>` symlink (e.g., into `/var/run/netns/` for `ip netns` management).

---

## 3. Union Filesystems & OverlayFS: Layer Storage

Container images act as layered archives providing a Copy-on-Write (CoW) unified filesystem view [[21:30](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1290)].

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Merged View (/merged)                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  UpperDir (Writable Container Layer)                    │
│    ├── Modified files (copied up)                       │
│    └── Whiteouts (char dev 0:0 for deleted files)       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LowerDir (Read-Only Image Layers, stacked)             │
│    ├── Layer 2 (Application code/diff)                 │
│    └── Layer 1 (Base OS / rootfs)                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

* **OverlayFS Components [[22:33](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1353)]:**
* `lowerdir`: Read-only base layers stacked sequentially.
* `upperdir`: Single read-write layer where runtime file changes land.
* `workdir`: Scratch directory used by the kernel for atomic operations during copy-up.
* `merged`: Mount target presenting the composite file tree.


* **Copy-Up Performance Cost [[23:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1380)]:** When a file in `lowerdir` is opened for writing, the entire file is copied up to `upperdir` before the `open()` syscall returns. Large files incur significant I/O latency and consume double disk space even if modifying a single byte.
* **Deletions & Whiteouts [[23:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1395)]:** Deleting a file from a lower layer does not remove it from disk; instead, OverlayFS writes a special character device (`0,0`) into `upperdir` to mask the lower file.
* **Docker Layout [[24:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1458)]:** Stored in `/var/lib/docker/overlay2/` using shortened layer symlinks (`/l/`) to stay within kernel mount option string length limits [[29:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1790)].

---

## 4. Container Runtimes & The OCI Standard

* **Container Runtime Definition [[31:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1860)]:** Host software that orchestrates cgroups, namespaces, and mounts to launch isolated processes.
* **OCI Runtime Specification [[31:23](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1883)]:** Standardized runtime interfaces and container bundle formats.
* **Bundle Structure [[31:51](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1911)]:** Consists of a root filesystem directory (`rootfs`) + a `config.json` file defining user, environment variables, capabilities, mounts, and lifecycle hooks.


* **Reference Implementation (`runc`) [[31:36](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1896)]:** Donated by Docker; used as the low-level executor by `containerd`, `CRI-O`, and Docker.
* **Lifecycle Hooks [[32:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1939)]:** Allows external tools to mutate filesystems or attach configurations before start (`prestart`), after start (`poststart`), and after exit (`poststop`).

---

## Quick Command & Troubleshooting Reference

| Objective | Command / Interface |
| --- | --- |
| Inspect cgroups of a running process | `cat /proc/<PID>/cgroup` [[06:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D363)] |
| Move process to a cgroup | `echo <PID> >> /sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/<group>/tasks` [[06:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D406)] |
| Inspect namespace symlinks | `ls -l /proc/<PID>/ns/` [[12:41](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D761)] |
| Run shell in isolated net namespace | `unshare --net /bin/bash` [[15:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D917)] |
| Enter container namespace from host | `nsenter --target <PID> --mount --net -- /bin/bash` [[19:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1186)] |
| Manage persistent net namespace | `ip netns add <name>` / `ip netns exec <name> <cmd>` [[16:25](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D985)] |

---

## Takeaways & Gotchas

* **Hidden disk bloat:** Removing files in upper Dockerfile layers does not reduce image size because lower layer data remains intact beneath whiteout markers [[27:42](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1662)].
* **Namespace lifetime gotcha:** If all processes inside a namespace exit and no bind mount exists, the namespace is immediately destroyed by the kernel [[15:35](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D935)].
* **Orchestrator dependencies:** Manually altering cgroup hierarchies on managed nodes can break metrics scrapers like cAdvisor or Amazon ECS agent [[09:54](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D594)].

## To Research / Backlog

* **cgroups v2 unified hierarchy:** Transition from independent subsystem trees to single unified hierarchy with improved resource delegation.
* **Rootless Containers & User Namespaces:** Mapping UID 0 inside a container to an unprivileged UID on the host for enhanced isolation.
* **Time Namespace:** Handling container virtualization of monotonic and boot system clocks [[10:56](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D656)].

## Thoughts / Philosophy

> *"Containers are not monolithic boxes created by virtualization; they are ordinary processes wearing kernel-provided blindfolds (namespaces) and speed limits (cgroups), standing on a layered stack of files (OverlayFS)."*

* **Bundle Structure [[31:51](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1911)]:** Consists of a root filesystem directory (`rootfs`) + a `config.json` file defining user, environment variables, capabilities, mounts, and lifecycle hooks.


* **Reference Implementation (`runc`) [[31:36](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1896)]:** Donated by Docker; used as the low-level executor by `containerd`, `CRI-O`, and Docker.
* **Lifecycle Hooks [[32:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1939)]:** Allows external tools to mutate filesystems or attach configurations before start (`prestart`), after start (`poststart`), and after exit (`poststop`).

---

## Quick Command & Troubleshooting Reference

| Objective | Command / Interface |
| --- | --- |
| Inspect cgroups of a running process | `cat /proc/<PID>/cgroup` [[06:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D363)] |
| Move process to a cgroup | `echo <PID> >> /sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/<group>/tasks` [[06:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D406)] |
| Inspect namespace symlinks | `ls -l /proc/<PID>/ns/` [[12:41](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D761)] |
| Run shell in isolated net namespace | `unshare --net /bin/bash` [[15:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D917)] |
| Enter container namespace from host | `nsenter --target <PID> --mount --net -- /bin/bash` [[19:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1186)] |
| Manage persistent net namespace | `ip netns add <name>` / `ip netns exec <name> <cmd>` [[16:25](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D985)] |

---

## Takeaways & Gotchas

* **Hidden disk bloat:** Removing files in upper Dockerfile layers does not reduce image size because lower layer data remains intact beneath whiteout markers [[27:42](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1662)].
* **Namespace lifetime gotcha:** If all processes inside a namespace exit and no bind mount exists, the namespace is immediately destroyed by the kernel [[15:35](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D935)].
* **Orchestrator dependencies:** Manually altering cgroup hierarchies on managed nodes can break metrics scrapers like cAdvisor or Amazon ECS agent [[09:54](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D594)].

## To Research / Backlog

* **cgroups v2 unified hierarchy:** Transition from independent subsystem trees to single unified hierarchy with improved resource delegation.
* **Rootless Containers & User Namespaces:** Mapping UID 0 inside a container to an unprivileged UID on the host for enhanced isolation.
* **Time Namespace:** Handling container virtualization of monotonic and boot system clocks [[10:56](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D656)].

## Thoughts / Philosophy

> *"Containers are not monolithic boxes created by virtualization; they are ordinary processes wearing kernel-provided blindfolds (namespaces) and speed limits (cgroups), standing on a layered stack of files (OverlayFS)."*

# Linux Container Primitives — Vault Notes

## The Core Mental Model

* **Containers do not exist as a single kernel primitive [[01:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D75)]:** A "container" is simply a standard Linux process isolated and constrained by combining three independent kernel primitives:
1. **Control Groups (cgroups):** Resource accounting, limits, and prioritization.
2. **Namespaces:** Visibility and access boundaries (what the process can see).
3. **Layered File Systems (OverlayFS):** Copy-on-write image composition and root filesystem isolation.



---

## 1. Control Groups (cgroups): Resource Management

cgroups track, group, and limit resource consumption across process trees [[02:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D139)]. Every process on a modern Linux system belongs to a cgroup hierarchy regardless of whether it runs in a container.

* **Subsystem Hierarchies [[02:49](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D169)]:** Subsystems (CPU, memory, pids, devices, blkio) maintain independent trees. This enables flexible configuration (e.g., two processes can share a memory pool while having unequal CPU shares).
* **Inheritance [[04:06](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D246)]:** Child processes automatically inherit the cgroup membership of their parent.
* **Virtual VFS Interface [[04:12](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D252)]:** Managed via `/sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/`.
* `tasks` / `cgroup.procs`: Holds assigned PIDs. Writing a PID into this file moves the target process into that cgroup [[04:43](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D283)].
* `pids.max`: Limits max concurrent processes to prevent resource exhaustion attacks like fork bombs [[07:34](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D454)].
* `cpu.shares`: Proportional weight for CPU time distribution [[09:01](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D541)].


* **Introspection [[05:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D348)]:** A process's assigned cgroups can be inspected at `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`.

---

## 2. Namespaces: Boundary & Visibility Control

Namespaces restrict what a process can see and access, creating the illusion that each container has its own dedicated system resources [[10:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D618)].

### Core Namespaces Used in Containers

* **Network (`net`) [[11:24](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D684)]:** Independent network devices, IP routing tables, port bindings, and firewall rules. Connected to host bridges (e.g., `docker0`) via virtual Ethernet (`veth`) pairs.
* **Mount (`mnt`) [[12:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D723)]:** Dedicated filesystem mount points, hiding the host filesystem and presenting an isolated rootfs.
* **PID (`pid`):** Independent process tree where the root container process runs as PID 1.
* User (`user`), IPC (`ipc`), UTS (`uts`), Time (`time`) [[10:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D650)].

### Namespace Syscalls & Lifecycle

* **`clone(..., CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:16](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D796)]:** Spawns a child process directly inside a new set of namespaces.
* **`unshare(CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:28](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D808)]:** Disassociates the calling process from its current namespaces and creates new ones.
* **`setns(fd, nstype)` [[14:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D857)]:** Attaches a process to an existing namespace using an open file descriptor from `/proc/<pid>/ns/*` or a persistent bind mount.
* **Persistence Mechanism [[13:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D828)]:** Namespaces terminate when no active processes or references remain. To keep an empty namespace alive, create a bind mount of its `/proc/<pid>/ns/<type>` symlink (e.g., into `/var/run/netns/` for `ip netns` management).

---

## 3. Union Filesystems & OverlayFS: Layer Storage

Container images act as layered archives providing a Copy-on-Write (CoW) unified filesystem view [[21:30](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1290)].

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Merged View (/merged)                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  UpperDir (Writable Container Layer)                    │
│    ├── Modified files (copied up)                       │
│    └── Whiteouts (char dev 0:0 for deleted files)       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LowerDir (Read-Only Image Layers, stacked)             │
│    ├── Layer 2 (Application code/diff)                 │
│    └── Layer 1 (Base OS / rootfs)                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

* **OverlayFS Components [[22:33](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1353)]:**
* `lowerdir`: Read-only base layers stacked sequentially.
* `upperdir`: Single read-write layer where runtime file changes land.
* `workdir`: Scratch directory used by the kernel for atomic operations during copy-up.
* `merged`: Mount target presenting the composite file tree.


* **Copy-Up Performance Cost [[23:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1380)]:** When a file in `lowerdir` is opened for writing, the entire file is copied up to `upperdir` before the `open()` syscall returns. Large files incur significant I/O latency and consume double disk space even if modifying a single byte.
* **Deletions & Whiteouts [[23:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1395)]:** Deleting a file from a lower layer does not remove it from disk; instead, OverlayFS writes a special character device (`0,0`) into `upperdir` to mask the lower file.
* **Docker Layout [[24:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1458)]:** Stored in `/var/lib/docker/overlay2/` using shortened layer symlinks (`/l/`) to stay within kernel mount option string length limits [[29:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1790)].

---

## 4. Container Runtimes & The OCI Standard

* **Container Runtime Definition [[31:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1860)]:** Host software that orchestrates cgroups, namespaces, and mounts to launch isolated processes.
* **OCI Runtime Specification [[31:23](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1883)]:** Standardized runtime interfaces and container bundle formats.
* **Bundle Structure [[31:51](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1911)]:** Consists of a root filesystem directory (`rootfs`) + a `config.json` file defining user, environment variables, capabilities, mounts, and lifecycle hooks.


* **Reference Implementation (`runc`) [[31:36](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1896)]:** Donated by Docker; used as the low-level executor by `containerd`, `CRI-O`, and Docker.
* **Lifecycle Hooks [[32:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1939)]:** Allows external tools to mutate filesystems or attach configurations before start (`prestart`), after start (`poststart`), and after exit (`poststop`).

---

## Quick Command & Troubleshooting Reference

| Objective | Command / Interface |
| --- | --- |
| Inspect cgroups of a running process | `cat /proc/<PID>/cgroup` [[06:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D363)] |
| Move process to a cgroup | `echo <PID> >> /sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/<group>/tasks` [[06:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D406)] |
| Inspect namespace symlinks | `ls -l /proc/<PID>/ns/` [[12:41](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D761)] |
| Run shell in isolated net namespace | `unshare --net /bin/bash` [[15:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D917)] |
| Enter container namespace from host | `nsenter --target <PID> --mount --net -- /bin/bash` [[19:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1186)] |
| Manage persistent net namespace | `ip netns add <name>` / `ip netns exec <name> <cmd>` [[16:25](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D985)] |

## Takeaways & Gotchas

* **Hidden disk bloat:** Removing files in upper Dockerfile layers does not reduce image size because lower layer data remains intact beneath whiteout markers [[27:42](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1662)].
* **Namespace lifetime gotcha:** If all processes inside a namespace exit and no bind mount exists, the namespace is immediately destroyed by the kernel [[15:35](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D935)].
* **Orchestrator dependencies:** Manually altering cgroup hierarchies on managed nodes can break metrics scrapers like cAdvisor or Amazon ECS agent [[09:54](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D594)].

## 3. Union Filesystems & OverlayFS: Layer Storage

Container images act as layered archives providing a Copy-on-Write (CoW) unified filesystem view [[21:30](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1290)].

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Merged View (/merged)                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  UpperDir (Writable Container Layer)                    │
│    ├── Modified files (copied up)                       │
│    └── Whiteouts (char dev 0:0 for deleted files)       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LowerDir (Read-Only Image Layers, stacked)             │
│    ├── Layer 2 (Application code/diff)                 │
│    └── Layer 1 (Base OS / rootfs)                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

* **OverlayFS Components [[22:33](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1353)]:**
* `lowerdir`: Read-only base layers stacked sequentially.
* `upperdir`: Single read-write layer where runtime file changes land.
* `workdir`: Scratch directory used by the kernel for atomic operations during copy-up.
* `merged`: Mount target presenting the composite file tree.


* **Copy-Up Performance Cost [[23:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1380)]:** When a file in `lowerdir` is opened for writing, the entire file is copied up to `upperdir` before the `open()` syscall returns. Large files incur significant I/O latency and consume double disk space even if modifying a single byte.
* **Deletions & Whiteouts [[23:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1395)]:** Deleting a file from a lower layer does not remove it from disk; instead, OverlayFS writes a special character device (`0,0`) into `upperdir` to mask the lower file.
* **Docker Layout [[24:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1458)]:** Stored in `/var/lib/docker/overlay2/` using shortened layer symlinks (`/l/`) to stay within kernel mount option string length limits [[29:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1790)].

---

## 4. Container Runtimes & The OCI Standard

* **Container Runtime Definition [[31:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1860)]:** Host software that orchestrates cgroups, namespaces, and mounts to launch isolated processes.
* **OCI Runtime Specification [[31:23](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1883)]:** Standardized runtime interfaces and container bundle formats.
* **Bundle Structure [[31:51](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1911)]:** Consists of a root filesystem directory (`rootfs`) + a `config.json` file defining user, environment variables, capabilities, mounts, and lifecycle hooks.


* **Reference Implementation (`runc`) [[31:36](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1896)]:** Donated by Docker; used as the low-level executor by `containerd`, `CRI-O`, and Docker.
* **Lifecycle Hooks [[32:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1939)]:** Allows external tools to mutate filesystems or attach configurations before start (`prestart`), after start (`poststart`), and after exit (`poststop`).

---

## Quick Command & Troubleshooting Reference

| Objective | Command / Interface |
| --- | --- |
| Inspect cgroups of a running process | `cat /proc/<PID>/cgroup` [[06:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D363)] |
| Move process to a cgroup | `echo <PID> >> /sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/<group>/tasks` [[06:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D406)] |
| Inspect namespace symlinks | `ls -l /proc/<PID>/ns/` [[12:41](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D761)] |
| Run shell in isolated net namespace | `unshare --net /bin/bash` [[15:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D917)] |
| Enter container namespace from host | `nsenter --target <PID> --mount --net -- /bin/bash` [[19:46](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1186)] |
| Manage persistent net namespace | `ip netns add <name>` / `ip netns exec <name> <cmd>` [[16:25](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D985)] |

---

## Takeaways & Gotchas

* **Hidden disk bloat:** Removing files in upper Dockerfile layers does not reduce image size because lower layer data remains intact beneath whiteout markers [[27:42](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1662)].
* **Namespace lifetime gotcha:** If all processes inside a namespace exit and no bind mount exists, the namespace is immediately destroyed by the kernel [[15:35](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D935)].
* **Orchestrator dependencies:** Manually altering cgroup hierarchies on managed nodes can break metrics scrapers like cAdvisor or Amazon ECS agent [[09:54](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D594)].

## To Research / Backlog

* **cgroups v2 unified hierarchy:** Transition from independent subsystem trees to single unified hierarchy with improved resource delegation.
* **Rootless Containers & User Namespaces:** Mapping UID 0 inside a container to an unprivileged UID on the host for enhanced isolation.
* **Time Namespace:** Handling container virtualization of monotonic and boot system clocks [[10:56](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D656)].

## Thoughts / Philosophy

> *"Containers are not monolithic boxes created by virtualization; they are ordinary processes wearing kernel-provided blindfolds (namespaces) and speed limits (cgroups), standing on a layered stack of files (OverlayFS)."*

* Linux Programmer's Manual: `man 7 namespaces`, `man 2 clone`, `man 2 setns`, `man 2 unshare` [[20:26](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1226)]
* Open Containers Initiative (OCI): Runtime & Image Specifications [[31:23](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1883)] your

# Linux Container Primitives — Vault Notes

## The Core Mental Model

* **Containers do not exist as a single kernel primitive [[01:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D75)]:** A "container" is simply a standard Linux process isolated and constrained by combining three independent kernel primitives:
1. **Control Groups (cgroups):** Resource accounting, limits, and prioritization.
2. **Namespaces:** Visibility and access boundaries (what the process can see).
3. **Layered File Systems (OverlayFS):** Copy-on-write image composition and root filesystem isolation.



---

## 1. Control Groups (cgroups): Resource Management

cgroups track, group, and limit resource consumption across process trees [[02:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D139)]. Every process on a modern Linux system belongs to a cgroup hierarchy regardless of whether it runs in a container.

* **Subsystem Hierarchies [[02:49](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D169)]:** Subsystems (CPU, memory, pids, devices, blkio) maintain independent trees. This enables flexible configuration (e.g., two processes can share a memory pool while having unequal CPU shares).
* **Inheritance [[04:06](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D246)]:** Child processes automatically inherit the cgroup membership of their parent.
* **Virtual VFS Interface [[04:12](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D252)]:** Managed via `/sys/fs/cgroup/<subsystem>/`.
* `tasks` / `cgroup.procs`: Holds assigned PIDs. Writing a PID into this file moves the target process into that cgroup [[04:43](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D283)].
* `pids.max`: Limits max concurrent processes to prevent resource exhaustion attacks like fork bombs [[07:34](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D454)].
* `cpu.shares`: Proportional weight for CPU time distribution [[09:01](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D541)].


* **Introspection [[05:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D348)]:** A process's assigned cgroups can be inspected at `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`.

---

## 2. Namespaces: Boundary & Visibility Control

Namespaces restrict what a process can see and access, creating the illusion that each container has its own dedicated system resources [[10:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D618)].

### Core Namespaces Used in Containers

* **Network (`net`) [[11:24](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D684)]:** Independent network devices, IP routing tables, port bindings, and firewall rules. Connected to host bridges (e.g., `docker0`) via virtual Ethernet (`veth`) pairs.
* **Mount (`mnt`) [[12:03](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D723)]:** Dedicated filesystem mount points, hiding the host filesystem and presenting an isolated rootfs.
* **PID (`pid`):** Independent process tree where the root container process runs as PID 1.
* User (`user`), IPC (`ipc`), UTS (`uts`), Time (`time`) [[10:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D650)].

### Namespace Syscalls & Lifecycle

* **`clone(..., CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:16](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D796)]:** Spawns a child process directly inside a new set of namespaces.
* **`unshare(CLONE_NEW*)` [[13:28](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D808)]:** Disassociates the calling process from its current namespaces and creates new ones.
* **`setns(fd, nstype)` [[14:17](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D857)]:** Attaches a process to an existing namespace using an open file descriptor from `/proc/<pid>/ns/*` or a persistent bind mount.
* **Persistence Mechanism [[13:48](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D828)]:** Namespaces terminate when no active processes or references remain. To keep an empty namespace alive, create a bind mount of its `/proc/<pid>/ns/<type>` symlink (e.g., into `/var/run/netns/` for `ip netns` management).

---

## 3. Union Filesystems & OverlayFS: Layer Storage

Container images act as layered archives providing a Copy-on-Write (CoW) unified filesystem view [[21:30](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1290)].

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Merged View (/merged)                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  UpperDir (Writable Container Layer)                    │
│    ├── Modified files (copied up)                       │
│    └── Whiteouts (char dev 0:0 for deleted files)       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  LowerDir (Read-Only Image Layers, stacked)             │
│    ├── Layer 2 (Application code/diff)                 │
│    └── Layer 1 (Base OS / rootfs)                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

* **OverlayFS Components [[22:33](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1353)]:**
* `lowerdir`: Read-only base layers stacked sequentially.
* `upperdir`: Single read-write layer where runtime file changes land.
* `workdir`: Scratch directory used by the kernel for atomic operations during copy-up.
* `merged`: Mount target presenting the composite file tree.


* **Copy-Up Performance Cost [[23:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1380)]:** When a file in `lowerdir` is opened for writing, the entire file is copied up to `upperdir` before the `open()` syscall returns. Large files incur significant I/O latency and consume double disk space even if modifying a single byte.
* **Deletions & Whiteouts [[23:15](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1395)]:** Deleting a file from a lower layer does not remove it from disk; instead, OverlayFS writes a special character device (`0,0`) into `upperdir` to mask the lower file.
* **Docker Layout [[24:18](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1458)]:** Stored in `/var/lib/docker/overlay2/` using shortened layer symlinks (`/l/`) to stay within kernel mount option string length limits [[29:50](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1790)].

## 4. Container Runtimes & The OCI Standard

* **Container Runtime Definition [[31:00](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1860)]:** Host software that orchestrates cgroups, namespaces, and mounts to launch isolated processes.
* **OCI Runtime Specification [[31:23](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1883)]:** Standardized runtime interfaces and container bundle formats.
* **Bundle Structure [[31:51](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1911)]:** Consists of a root filesystem directory (`rootfs`) + a `config.json` file defining user, environment variables, capabilities, mounts, and lifecycle hooks.


* **Reference Implementation (`runc`) [[31:36](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1896)]:** Donated by Docker; used as the low-level executor by `containerd`, `CRI-O`, and Docker.
* **Lifecycle Hooks [[32:19](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dx1npPrzyKfs%26t%3D1939)]:** Allows external tools to mutate filesystems or attach configurations before start (`prestart`), after start (`poststart`), and after exit (`poststop`).
